ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A ghost cave is a dark, dead enclosure in which someone settles and tries to make a livelihood.
EvidenceBody: Chan speakers bend the literal cave into a verdict on being trapped in blank stillness, fixed understanding, or the very attempt to lodge in neither coming nor going. Dahui Zonggao applies it to students who suppress movement and then sit unable to turn; other commentators say a formulation leads people into 'making a livelihood in a ghost cave.' The phrase condemns an enclosed dead end—it does not name a productive retreat.
